Decision_Tree.technical_reason: Spark DecisionTreeClassifier uses approximate histogram binning (maxBins=32 by default) to distribute feature splitting across cluster nodes, whereas scikit-learn DecisionTreeClassifier performs exact continuous threshold optimization across all unique feature values. On network flow distributions with extreme outliers (Flow Duration, Flow Bytes/s), 32 quantile bins collapse subtle decision boundaries.

Naive_Bayes.technical_reason: Spark MLlib NaiveBayes modelType='gaussian' computes variance thresholds per partition without scikit-learn's global var_smoothing regularization. Additionally, Spark uses partition-level aggregation while scikit-learn computes exact in-memory sample moments.
